summary: Hardens identifier and string-literal emission against injection: backslash escaping in eight SQL dialects and, by default, in the unknown-product ANSI fallback (with a system property to opt out); identifier quoting or validation in the Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Geode, MongoDB and Splunk adapters.

tests.evidence: Behavior changes across many dialects and adapters. CassandraIdentifierQuotingTest tests only the driver's CqlIdentifier, not CassandraTable.query, so it cannot fail if Calcite stops using it. The Splunk test invoked a private method by reflection, which the reviewer questioned and the author changed.

user_docs.evidence: New system property calcite.sql.dialect.unknown.escapes.backslash and a changed default for the fallback dialect. Documented in CalciteSystemProperty Javadoc and a site/_docs/history.md breaking-change entry.

doc_comments.evidence: Many new comments and Javadoc. Reviewer asked for Elasticsearch helpers to be renamed or re-documented (JSON versus script language, escapeJsonString), for an explanation of the possessive quantifier, for GeodeUtils Javadoc to stop naming callers, and for a misplaced Cassandra comment to be moved.

change_description.evidence: The history.md entry is present. The PR body lists what changed but not why (statement-boundary injection), and the title says only 'improve'.

performance.evidence: String escaping and regex validation at query-generation time; not a hot path.

security.evidence: The purpose is quoting and escaping to stop values or identifiers from breaking out of generated SQL, CQL, OQL, JSON, Painless or Splunk text; each escaping rule needs a check against the target lexer.

backward_compat.evidence: Changes generated SQL for eight dialects and changes the default for unknown products. On a standards-lexing backend the fallback now alters data values ('a\b' becomes 'a\\b'), and Geode queries with non-simple identifiers now fail instead of being pushed down.

concurrency.evidence: No shared state or lifecycle changes.

error_model.evidence: New rejection paths. GeodeUtils.checkSafeOqlIdentifier throws a bare RuntimeException, while GeodeTable.checkOql and the GeodeRules paths throw IllegalArgumentException for the same class of problem.

correctness.evidence: Non-trivial escaping and regex validators, and the escaped regex in Hive and Spark TRIM (RelToSqlConverterTest). The reviewer called it very complicated and did not verify the per-dialect rules.

user_value.evidence: A hardening fix with no new API apart from the opt-out property.

surprising_behavior.evidence: The unknown-dialect fallback now doubles backslashes by default. The Javadoc says that on standard backends this is at worst rendered verbatim, which means string values silently change and WHERE comparisons against them may return different rows.

contradictions.evidence: Two Geode validators disagree on exception type. The Netezza comment says backslash escapes apply unless standard-conforming-strings is on, yet the dialect doubles them unconditionally.

build_ci.evidence: No build or dependency changes; the Cassandra test uses the existing driver dependency.

observability.evidence: Refusals to push down surface as planner fallback or exceptions; there is no retry or fallback that needs a log.

spec_conformance.evidence: Each dialect's escaping interprets that database's lexical spec; the author cited vendor docs, but the reviewer did not verify them. Netezza escaping depends on the session option, and BigQuery and ClickHouse identifier backslash rules need checking.

plan.why: A broad injection-hardening change over many dialects and adapters: escaping correctness against each target's spec is one focus, and compatibility, defaults and documentation of the new behavior are another.
